translations.answer: The thread and merged PR #209/#210 divide responsibilities into two layers: the `prepareSwitch()` in non-realtime callbacks handles potentially time-consuming preparation and feasibility checks; the `doSwitch()` and controller start/stop occur in the real-time `update()` path and must be non-blocking. This prevents hardware mode from changing prematurely while the controller is still switching. For hardware requiring multiple cycle confirmations, the thread does not provide a general strategy, and the driver must explicitly handle old/new command processing during the switch period.
translations.applicability: Directly applicable to ROS 1 Indigo/Jade historical interfaces; modern ros2_control must recheck against the current lifecycle/switch API.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and free of conflicts, and there is formal documentation or precise independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: PR #209/#210 save the start/stop list, move `doSwitch()` to real-time `update()`, and use non-realtime `prepareSwitch()` for blocking preparation.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Audit the thread and actual order of `prepareSwitch()`/`doSwitch()`/controller start/stop, and record the cycle time required for hardware mode confirmation.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use a two-phase interface: `prepareSwitch()` non-realtime preparation + `doSwitch()` real-time, non-blocking submission.
translations.details.environments.0: ROS 1 ros_control Indigo/Jade; author has hardware replication; ros_canopen participants reported typical switch cycle time of 3–4 cycles, with some hardware requiring over 5 cycles.
translations.details.limits.0: This is the historical ROS 1 Indigo/Jade interface; slow hardware still needs to define command retention, discard, and synchronization strategies during the switch period.
translations.details.limits.1: There was debate over whether the thread could handle multiple cycle switches; the final merged solution does not equate to any hardware being able to complete a physical mode switch in a single cycle.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #209 and #210 merged; #209 passed testing after revision; ros_canopen participants confirmed the Indigo change works as expected.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why can't hardware control mode be switched before the controller completes the switch?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How should slow hardware coexist with a single-cycle controller switch semantics?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: True machine mode switching should first validate in the hoist/empty and low-gain conditions, monitoring old/new commands, hardware mode acknowledgment, and emergency stop status; do not block the bus during real-time `doSwitch()`.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: `doSwitch()` is incorrectly placed in the only non-realtime ROS callback responsible for scheduling the switch, while controller start/stop actually occur in the real-time `update()` thread.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Old implementations may switch hardware mode before starting the new controller, leading to commands being in the wrong mode or undefined behavior.

translations.source.title: Controller Mode Switching: prepareSwitch and doSwitch Must Be in Separate Realtime and Nonrealtime Stages
translations.title: When Should `prepareSwitch()` and `doSwitch()` Be Executed in ROS Control?
